about.title: Seeing education from three sides
about.lead: I'm Victoria Naumenko. I work at a school in Russia — and I build the tools I wish I'd had in everyday teaching.
paragraphs: I'm a deputy head of school, an English teacher of the highest qualification category, a teacher of Russian as a foreign and as an additional language, and a mentor to colleagues. These roles let me see education through the eyes of a learner, a teacher and a school leader.
My projects grow out of real school questions: how to make vocabulary practice engaging, how to help teachers hear each other, and how to make AI a genuinely useful assistant for a teacher.

roles.text: Russian as a foreign and as an additional language, plus English. I look for ways to make every topic clear and practice accessible to learners with different backgrounds.
As a deputy head, I connect school-wide goals with teachers' day-to-day work and help turn plans into clear actions.
I work through difficult situations with colleagues, share experience and help them find their own professional solutions.
I design educational games and digital tools. I test what AI can do and judge it by how useful it is for teachers and learners.

about.quote_text: AI tools can make preparation easier. Understanding the learner, checking materials and taking responsibility stay with the teacher.

items.title: PEDAGOG
items.description: One school situation, several professional perspectives. At first only two or three roles see the case; then new circumstances emerge and more voices join in — a classmate, a form tutor, a parent, a school psychologist, the leadership team. The game helps teachers hear different positions, separate facts from first impressions and find a solution together.
facts: minutes — online or at the table
items.audience: For teachers, form tutors, mentors and school leaders
items.alt: PEDAGOG home page: “Real situations. Different roles. New solutions”

items.title: LEXIGO
items.description: Vocabulary from the Spotlight textbooks turned into short, game-based practice. Learners pick a textbook and lesson, then train words in the mode they like: flashcards, multiple choice, spelling, audio dictation, matching and a final test. Teachers can print A4 quizzes.
items.audience: For school students and teachers of English
items.note: Interface in Russian. An independent project, not an official product of the textbook publisher.
items.alt: LEXIGO screen: choosing a Spotlight textbook
